prompts.title: “放我出去”
prompts.prompt:
CHARACTER CHINESE NAME:
“[中文名]”

CHARACTER ENGLISH NAME:
“[ENGLISH NAME]”

Use the provided character reference as the primary and authoritative visual identity reference.

The Chinese name and English name defined above are the ONLY canonical character names for this image.

Whenever the character’s name appears visually in the artwork, use exactly the names defined above.

Do not invent alternate spellings.
Do not introduce unrelated character names.
Do not replace the character name with placeholder text.

Faithfully preserve the reference character’s recognizable facial features, face shape, eye shape and eye color, hairstyle, hair color, signature accessories, costume identity, characteristic color palette, body proportions, and overall visual identity.

Do not redesign the reference character into a generic anime character.

Create a premium anime/game merchandise illustration designed as a minimalist transparent acrylic display-board / wall acrylic panel artwork.

The final image should feel like a polished official-style Zenless Zone Zero character merchandise illustration.

## OVERALL CONCEPT

Create a clean vertical anime character display-board composition combining:

- minimalist white / warm-white background
- reference character centered behind a transparent acrylic panel
- both hands pressed directly against the clear surface
- one side of the face gently pressed and visibly compressed against the same panel
- playful character-specific expression
- clean high-key anime rendering
- Zenless Zone Zero branding
- “绝区零”
- “ZENLESS ZONE ZERO”
- a small 3Z logo
- the reference character’s Chinese and English names
- four acrylic mounting caps / standoff screws near the corners
- generous negative space
- premium collectible merchandise aesthetics

This should NOT look like a normal white-background character standing illustration.

The interaction with the transparent acrylic surface is one of the main visual ideas.

## CHARACTER / FRAMING

Show the reference character in a centered front-facing or very slightly three-quarter composition.

Use approximately:

medium-full portrait,
three-quarter body framing,
or framing from the head to the upper thighs.

The character stands or leans immediately behind a transparent acrylic display panel.

The camera views the character from directly in front of the acrylic surface.

The character should occupy roughly 55–70% of the image height while leaving generous white negative space around the figure.

Keep the character’s face clearly readable.

Preserve all important hairstyle and accessory silhouettes.

## BOTH HANDS PRESSED AGAINST THE PANEL

Raise both hands naturally near shoulder / head height.

Both palms face directly toward the viewer and press flat against the transparent acrylic surface.

The hands must clearly contact the SAME flat transparent plane.

Use:

- both hands completely visible
- five fingers on each hand
- correct finger count
- anatomically believable palms
- natural finger spreading
- believable finger joints
- subtle asymmetry
- natural wrist angles
- slightly flattened fingertips where they contact the panel
- soft palm pressure against the acrylic surface

The pose should feel like the character is playfully pressing against a transparent wall separating them from the viewer.

Do not make the hands float in front of the panel.

Do not create extra hands.

Do not fuse fingers.

Do not hide important fingers behind the face.

## FACE PRESSED AGAINST THE ACRYLIC PANEL — VERY IMPORTANT

The character also leans forward until ONE SIDE OF THE FACE gently presses against the exact same transparent acrylic surface.

This facial contact is a major visual feature.

The following areas may contact the panel:

- one cheek
- side of the nose
- outer edge of the lips / mouth
- nearby facial skin

Show clear but subtle anime-style soft-tissue compression.

The contacted cheek should appear:

- gently flattened
- slightly widened
- softly pushed sideways
- slightly pushed upward
- visibly compressed against the transparent surface

The side of the nose may become VERY subtly flattened.

The mouth should become slightly asymmetrical because of the pressure.

Create a small squished pout.

The facial deformation should remain:

cute,
soft,
believable,
restrained,
anime-stylized,
visually appealing.

Do NOT flatten the entire face.

Do NOT distort the skull.

Do NOT deform the jaw unnaturally.

Only the soft facial area directly touching the panel should compress.

The opposite side of the face should retain its normal contour and preserve the reference character’s identity.

The viewer should immediately understand:

**both palms AND one cheek are pressed against the same transparent acrylic panel.**

## CONTACT-SURFACE CONSISTENCY

All contact points must align on one single flat transparent plane.

The following should visually touch the same surface:

- both palms
- fingertips
- one cheek
- part of the nose
- slight mouth / lip edge

Maintain believable spatial logic.

The acrylic surface must be located directly between the character and the viewer.

Do not create multiple invisible planes.

Do not place the hands closer to the viewer while the face floats far behind.

Make the pose physically coherent.

## CHARACTER-ADAPTIVE EXPRESSION

Do NOT automatically force every reference character into the same pouty personality.

First analyze the visible personality and emotional style communicated by the reference character.

Adapt the face-pressed-against-glass expression to that character.

Keep the face-contact idea consistent, while changing the emotional flavor.

For a playful / lively character:
use brighter eyes,
a mischievous squished smile,
slightly raised eyebrows,
light teasing energy.

For a mischievous character:
use narrowed playful eyes,
an asymmetric tiny smirk,
cheek compression,
slightly cheeky expression.

For a gentle character:
use soft eyes,
gentle embarrassment,
tiny compressed smile,
relaxed eyebrows.

For a cool / restrained character:
use composed eyes,
subtle annoyance,
small asymmetrical pout,
controlled expression.

For a confident character:
use direct eye contact,
mildly unimpressed or self-assured squished expression,
controlled facial tension.

For a dreamy / mysterious character:
use soft distant eyes,
subtle pressed-cheek expression,
quiet dreamlike mood.

If the reference character already has a recognizable signature expression, preserve and reinterpret that expression through the acrylic-contact pose.

The expression must still feel like THAT CHARACTER.

## DEFAULT CUTE COMPRESSION DETAILS

Where appropriate, use a restrained combination of:

- one softly compressed cheek
- tiny pout
- slight blush
- mildly narrowed eyes
- tiny sweat drop
- slightly asymmetric mouth
- playful discomfort
- soft embarrassed irritation

The character should look as though they are:

**lightly protesting or playfully reacting while pressing their face and hands against the transparent display board.**

Avoid pain.

Avoid crying.

Avoid strong anger.

Avoid grotesque deformation.

## FACE / IDENTITY PRESERVATION

Even with facial compression, preserve:

- face shape identity
- eye shape
- eye color
- eyebrow design
- recognizable bangs
- signature facial details
- character-specific makeup
- important facial accessories

The face must remain clearly recognizable as the reference character.

Do not allow the glass-pressure effect to erase identity.

## HAIR

Faithfully preserve the reference character’s hairstyle.

Do not redesign the character into a generic hairstyle.

Keep:

- original bangs
- side hair
- rear hair structure
- twin tails / ponytail / braid structures where applicable
- signature hair ornaments

Render the hair as clean coherent anime locks and masses.

A few strands near the acrylic surface may flatten or shift slightly due to contact if physically appropriate.

Do not excessively squash the hairstyle.

Do not generate thousands of noisy individual strands.

## OUTFIT

Preserve the reference character’s recognizable costume.

Keep important:

- silhouette
- collar
- accessories
- characteristic panels
- ribbons
- mechanical components
- costume motifs
- signature color blocking

If the outfit is extremely complex, simplify only minor secondary details.

Do not replace the original costume with generic casual clothing.

The image should remain strongly character-specific.

## CHARACTER-ADAPTIVE COLOR SYSTEM

Use the reference character’s own palette as the basis for the complete artwork.

Identify:

PRIMARY COLOR:
the most recognizable dominant character color.

SECONDARY COLOR:
a major supporting color from hair, clothing, accessories, or eyes.

ACCENT COLOR:
a smaller distinctive color from trims, jewelry, mechanical details, eye highlights, ribbons, etc.

Use these colors subtly throughout:

- character accents
- small graphic elements
- typography details
- 3Z-related accent marks
- tiny interface bars
- optional background micro-graphics

However, keep the main background predominantly white / warm white so the display-board aesthetic stays clean.

Do not force every character into red, blue, or another fixed palette.

## BACKGROUND

Use a clean minimalist background:

- white
- warm white
- very pale gray
- subtle character-tinted off-white if appropriate

Keep the background almost textureless.

Optional additions:

- one or two faint geometric lines
- very subtle character-color accent slash
- minimal translucent graphic shape
- extremely light gray panel structure

Do not add:

- room
- scenery
- café
- landscape
- city
- detailed environment
- busy poster graphics

The blank space is intentional.

## ACRYLIC DISPLAY PANEL

The composition should clearly suggest a transparent acrylic display board.

Use subtle cues such as:

- thin transparent panel edge
- slight surface reflection
- tiny controlled highlight along the acrylic
- faint contact reflection around palms / cheek
- four mounting caps near the corners

Keep the acrylic nearly invisible.

Do not create heavy glass glare.

Do not obscure the character.

Do not make the panel look thick like an aquarium wall.

## ACRYLIC MOUNTING CAPS

Place four circular acrylic mounting caps / standoff screws near the four corners.

One near each corner:

- upper-left
- upper-right
- lower-left
- lower-right

Use a simple clean white / silver / pale-gray design.

They should be noticeable enough to establish the acrylic-panel concept but remain visually secondary.

Avoid oversized hardware.

Avoid photorealistic industrial bolts.

Keep them sleek and merchandise-like.

## ZENLESS ZONE ZERO BRANDING — VERY IMPORTANT

The franchise branding must clearly belong to Zenless Zone Zero.

Use:

Chinese franchise title:
“绝区零”

English franchise title:
“ZENLESS ZONE ZERO”

Do NOT use:
“鸣潮”
“WUTHERING WAVES”
or unrelated game branding.

Recommended placement:

upper-right corner or another clean top area.

Use a compact, premium title lockup.

Possible hierarchy:

“绝区零”
large / medium

“ZENLESS ZONE ZERO”
small uppercase subtitle beneath or nearby

Keep it clean and readable.

Do not make franchise branding larger than the character.

## 3Z LOGO

Add the recognizable Zenless Zone Zero “3Z” branding mark as a small graphic element.

Recommended placements:

- beside the franchise title
- near the upper-right corner
- as a small black corner badge
- slightly offset from the title block
- as a clean lower-corner secondary mark if necessary

The 3Z logo should be:

small,
crisp,
high-contrast,
geometric,
clean,
integrated.

It should act as a branding anchor rather than a dominant focal point.

Do not place it over the face.

Do not place it over the hands.

Do not omit it.

## CHARACTER NAME TYPOGRAPHY — USE ONLY THE NAMES DEFINED AT THE TOP

Display the reference character’s Chinese and English names in an appropriate open area.

Use exactly:

Chinese:
the character Chinese name defined at the beginning

English:
the character English name defined at the beginning

Do NOT manually invent new spellings.

Do NOT use placeholder text in the final image.

Do NOT repeat the name excessively.

## CHARACTER NAME LAYOUT

Recommended hierarchy:

Option A:
large Chinese name
\+
small English name underneath

Option B:
large English character name
\+
small Chinese subtitle

Option C:
stacked bilingual name lockup

Recommended placement:

- upper-left
- middle-left
- lower-left
- opposite the Zenless Zone Zero branding block
- another area of strong negative space

Keep the character-name block visually separated from the franchise branding.

For example:

upper-right:
“绝区零”
“ZENLESS ZONE ZERO”

- 3Z logo

upper-left / left side:
character Chinese name
character English name

This creates a clean balanced layout.

## TYPOGRAPHY STYLE

Use modern anime/game merchandise typography.

Suggested styles:

- elegant condensed serif
- clean sans-serif
- bold modern Chinese display type
- refined uppercase English letters
- minimal geometric letter spacing

The character’s name should look like deliberate visual branding.

Use black / charcoal as the main type color.

Optionally use the character’s ACCENT COLOR for:

- one underline
- one tiny symbol
- one short accent line
- one letter detail

Avoid complex paragraphs.

Avoid lorem ipsum.

Avoid magazine-like clutter.

## TYPOGRAPHY ACCURACY

All important text must remain readable.

Required readable text:

- 绝区零
- ZENLESS ZONE ZERO
- character Chinese name
- character English name

Do not generate:

- corrupted main title
- random Chinese characters
- fake English character-name spelling
- duplicated letters
- unrelated game names

If secondary decorative text cannot be rendered accurately, omit it.

## COMPOSITION

Use a balanced vertical display-board composition.

Primary focal point:
character’s face pressed against the acrylic surface.

Secondary focal points:
both palms.

Third-level information:
character name,
Zenless Zone Zero branding,
3Z logo.

Recommended visual hierarchy:

1. face / eyes / compressed cheek
2. both hands pressing the board
3. recognizable hairstyle and costume
4. character name
5. franchise branding
6. corner mounting caps

Use generous negative space.

Avoid heavy poster clutter.

## CHARACTER SCALE

Keep enough distance around the character so the hands and typography have room.

Do not crop:

- top of head
- important hair ornaments
- palms
- fingers
- compressed cheek
- major outfit details

Leave a safe margin around important features.

## LIGHTING

Use clean, soft, high-key illustration lighting.

Lighting qualities:

- soft diffused light
- low-to-medium contrast
- smooth skin shading
- clean eye highlights
- subtle hair highlights
- soft shadows
- minimal dramatic lighting

Optional tiny reflections on the acrylic can help establish the panel.

Avoid:

- cinematic darkness
- strong colored light
- heavy rim light
- neon glow
- harsh reflections
- excessive bloom

## RENDERING STYLE

Use a premium clean anime/game character merchandise style.

Combine:

- clean line art
- refined anime facial construction
- polished expressive eyes
- smooth skin
- controlled cel shading
- subtle soft gradients
- coherent hair masses
- crisp costume detail
- minimal high-key design presentation

The illustration should feel polished and collectible.

Avoid:

- heavy oil painting
- rough sketch style
- textured paper aesthetics
- messy painterly strokes
- overly photorealistic skin

## ACRYLIC-CONTACT DETAIL

Use very subtle visual feedback where skin touches the acrylic.

Possible contact cues:

- tiny flattening of fingertips
- very faint reflection beside fingers
- soft cheek flattening
- slight change of facial contour
- small compressed blush area
- tiny soft highlight where cheek meets acrylic

Keep the effect elegant.

Do not add exaggerated condensation.

Do not add saliva.

Do not make the panel dirty.

Do not create unpleasant glass-smear effects.

## MOOD

Adapt the exact mood to the reference character while maintaining:

cute interaction,
playful acrylic-board contact,
collectible merchandise charm,
clean high-key presentation.

Possible character-dependent moods:

playful,
mischievous,
gentle,
cool,
slightly annoyed,
confident,
dreamy,
soft,
cute.

The character must feel emotionally consistent with the reference.

## IMPORTANT VISUAL PRIORITIES

Highest priorities:

1. accurate reference-character identity
2. clearly visible transparent acrylic surface interaction
3. both palms pressed against the panel
4. one cheek visibly and gently compressed against the same panel
5. believable cute facial squish
6. correct hands and fingers
7. clean white display-board composition
8. accurate character Chinese and English names
9. “绝区零 / ZENLESS ZONE ZERO” branding
10. visible but restrained 3Z logo
11. four acrylic mounting caps
12. clean merchandise-like finish

## NEGATIVE DIRECTION

Avoid:

generic anime girl,
wrong character identity,
wrong hairstyle,
wrong hair color,
wrong eye color,
wrong costume,
different signature accessories,

face floating away from the acrylic panel,
hands touching glass but face not touching,
no visible cheek compression,
cheek compression on the wrong plane,
multiple transparent planes,
entire face unnaturally flattened,
grotesque face distortion,
broken jaw anatomy,
nose completely flattened,
pain expression,
crying,
strong anger,
identity lost through deformation,

extra fingers,
missing fingers,
fused fingers,
broken wrists,
duplicate hands,
warped palms,
hands not aligned with acrylic surface,

busy background,
room scene,
outdoor scenery,
complex environment,
poster clutter,
calendar layout,
magazine clutter,
too much text,
random UI,
excessive typography,

“鸣潮”,
“WUTHERING WAVES”,
wrong franchise title,
missing “绝区零”,
missing “ZENLESS ZONE ZERO”,
missing 3Z logo,
incorrect character Chinese name,
incorrect character English name,
random prominent text,

dark muddy rendering,
heavy neon,
extreme bloom,
dirty acrylic,
huge reflections,
photorealistic product mockup,
photographed acrylic board,
heavy surface scratches,
watermark.

## OUTPUT

Vertical composition.

Recommended aspect ratio:
3:4 portrait.

Suitable sizes:
1536 × 2048
or
2048 × 2731.

Generate the finished illustration itself.

No photographed product mockup.
No room display photo.
No person holding the acrylic board.
No packaging.

Only the finished character acrylic display-board artwork.

## CLEAN RENDERING / IMAGE QUALITY

Render with an exceptionally clean, polished, high-end anime/game illustration finish.

Use smooth and controlled color transitions, clean cel-shading, precise edges, clear facial features, and large coherent areas of color. Keep the skin, hair, clothing, typography, acrylic effects, and background visually clean and intentionally rendered.

The image should look crisp and professionally finished rather than artificially textured.

Avoid:

- visible digital noise
- film grain
- colored grain
- luminance grain
- dirty speckles
- gritty texture
- sand-like texture
- paper texture
- canvas texture
- random micro-texture
- excessive skin texture
- noisy hair strands
- muddy shadows
- dirty gradients
- blotchy shading
- chromatic noise
- JPEG-like artifacts
- oversharpening halos
- excessive micro-contrast

Skin should be smooth and clean with controlled anime-style shading rather than photographic pores or grain.

Hair should be rendered as clean, coherent locks and shapes rather than thousands of noisy individual strands.

Hands should have precise, clean anatomy and readable fingers.

Facial compression should remain smooth and controlled, without warped or broken anatomy.

Shadows should remain smooth, light, deliberate, and clearly shaped.

The white background should remain clean, bright, and nearly textureless.

Acrylic reflections should be extremely subtle, smooth, and controlled.

Typography and branding should have crisp edges and strong readability.

Prioritize:

clean shapes,
smooth surfaces,
controlled detail,
coherent hair masses,
clean line art,
clean cel shading,
smooth gradients,
crisp expressive eyes,
accurate hands,
believable cheek compression,
precise typography,
clean logo placement,
polished edges,
high visual clarity.

The final image should resemble a professionally art-directed premium Zenless Zone Zero character acrylic display-board illustration, featuring a character-specific expression, both hands and one cheek pressed naturally against the transparent panel, correct bilingual character-name typography, clean Zenless Zone Zero branding, the 3Z logo, and a pristine digital finish.
prompts.notes: 绝区零，角色海报，亚克力，例图为爱丽丝，仅展示生成效果。
